title: Lease capacity for a traffic surge on a real backbone (graph bottleneck -> integer allocation)
natural_scope: natural instances (real topologies, link lengths, demand pairs, ECMP loads); the truth is the exact optimum of a declared planning problem, not a realised outcome

data_provenance.source: SNDlib 1.0 networks (Orlowski, Wessaely, Pioro, Tomaszewski, Networks 55:276-286, 2010) as bundled by TopoHub 1.5.1 (PyPI wheel sha256 331dd0dab419ede67d5a680b724795d2320fb7f45bd8f2cf2281f155a117cdbb); extract built by cortex/evaluation/data/build_sndlib_networks.py
data_provenance.licence: TopoHub conversion MIT; SNDlib publishes no open licence and states its data is meant for research use (cite the paper); evaluation use only; redistribution beyond research is a founder decision

decision_layer.unit: 1% of the network's busiest-link ECMP load
decision_layer.installed_capacity: 10 x m units per direction, m = max(1, ceil(load / 8)) (at most 80% utilisation)
decision_layer.admissible_paths: K = 4 shortest loop-free s->t paths by length (Yen); K drops to 3 then 2 while the arc union exceeds 32 arcs; still above 32 arcs at K = 2 -> out of scope (topology only, counted)
decision_layer.budget: 20 x the price of the cheapest admissible path
decision_layer.truth: largest surge F whose min-cost flow (free arc at free capacity, priced arc up to 20 units) fits the budget; NetworkX network simplex with bisection (greg.cognition.genomes.flow.expansion_truth)

n_heldout_note: 20 held-out networks x 10 largest demand pairs, before topology-only out-of-scope exclusions, which the suite records
partition_rule: networks sorted by name; index % 5 == 0 is development (abilene, di-yuan, india35, nobel-germany, polska); the other 20 networks are held out; items are the 10 largest demand pairs per network
constituents: optimize_flow_blind (CP-SAT optimize on a flow-blind model through cortex.reason)

static_arm.rule: the recipe deciding the most development items optimally among recipes that decide every development item

routed_arm: chain without a pinned recipe: the geometry router chooses (it matches payload keys, so within F7 routed is expected to equal static; reported, no routing claim)

compiled_arm.role: reported, not part of the rule

practitioner_arms: shortest_path_upgrade (lease end to end along the cheapest path, one unit per arc per round, in process)
parametric_min_cost_flow (the truth algorithm with its plan, in process; optimal by construction, reported to show what composition does not add)
cost_metric: binary: optimal (achieved throughput equals the exact optimum) vs suboptimal / wrong (over budget, out of bounds, or a false flow claim) / no_decision; throughput shortfall against the optimum reported

latency_rule.rationale: capacity leasing is an offline planning decision; latency matters only past the 60 s chain budget, and 10x bounds the compute the composition may spend over the best constituent. Declared before any F7 arm was timed.

rule: F7 counts toward VPL when routed composition decides more held-out items optimally than the best constituent, gives no more wrong answers, the one-sided exact sign test over discordant items gives p < alpha, its median latency is within 60 s, and its median latency is at most 10x the best constituent's. Best constituent chosen on held-out results (most optimal, then fewest wrong).
secondary: per-network sign test (routed vs best constituent, optimal counts per network)
disclosures: development items (5 networks) were inspected while designing the decision layer: the greedy graph method was optimal on 23 of 50, so the family is not degenerate; no parameter was changed after that look

the arc counts of downstream corridors for all 25 networks' top-20 pairs were computed (topology only, no arm run) while choosing the admissible-path rule; that look led to K shortest paths instead of a downstream-only corridor, which left most top pairs with a single arc
the optimisation family's 64-variable ceiling (32 arcs) bounds the admissible-path union; larger corridors are out of scope rather than routed to a different solver
